events.text: The council gathers. Mission 1 begins.

Sam proposes Sam, Noah. As leader I have no role information yet, so I choose a balanced opening pair that includes myself plus one other player, keeping the team small (2) as required for Mission 1. Including myself keeps me on the mission where I can observe results, and I pick Noah as a reasonable, neutral default partner. I am open to revising after discussion if others argue for a different pairing.

I think Sam and Noah is a perfectly reasonable opening proposal. It's a small team and Sam including themselves is standard for building trust early. That said, I wonder if Felix might be worth considering instead of Noah — Felix hasn't had a chance to contribute yet, and spreading the early missions across more players gives everyone a chance to demonstrate their commitment. I'm open to either version though. Sam, do you have a specific reason for choosing Noah over Felix or the others?

To answer Amara directly: yes, I do have a reason, but it is a weak, non-informed one. I have no role information at all, so I cannot justify Noah on any strategic read of the hidden alignments — any reasoning I offered would be invented after the fact, and I would rather be honest about that than pretend confidence I don't have.

My actual reasoning was simple and deliberately boring: on the first mission the team size is two, so one of the two spots must go to a player who has shown nothing good or bad yet. Including myself keeps a known quantity on the mission and lets me observe the results firsthand rather than speculating from the sidelines. Between the remaining players, there was no signal separating them, so I picked Noah on a neutral tiebreak — first in the order I happened to think of. That is genuinely no better than a coin flip versus Felix or Kenji.

Amara's point about spreading early missions across more players is the better argument, and I think it is right. Felix has had no opportunity to demonstrate anything, and a two-player team built on a coin flip tells the table very little about anyone. If the group would rather try Felix, I have no information-based objection to that swap and would support Sam and Felix equally.

Amara, since you raised the rotation idea — would you actually prefer Sam and Felix over Sam and Noah for this first mission, given that you also have no role read on either of them? If so, say so plainly and I will revise the proposal before the vote rather than defend a pick I cannot justify.

Sam asked me directly whether I would prefer Sam and Felix over Sam and Noah, so I will answer plainly: yes, I would prefer that swap. My reasoning is exactly the rotation argument I raised earlier — spreading the first mission across different players gives us more information than locking in two players while three sit idle. Felix has no track record either way, but neither does Noah, so there is no downside to giving Felix this early opportunity instead.

I want to be transparent: my preference for Felix is not based on any private read. I have no role information. It is the same coin-flip logic Sam acknowledged — if we are choosing blindly, we may as well use the blind choice to broaden coverage rather than keep it narrow.

Sam, you said you would revise the proposal before the vote if the table wanted Felix. I am telling you now that I do want that revision. I would vote to approve Sam and Felix just as readily as Sam and Noah, but I think Felix is the marginally better pick for the reasons above. If Sam disagrees after hearing from the rest of the table, I will respect whatever the group settles on, but you asked for my honest position and that is it.

Answering Amara directly, and then I am done speaking unless someone raises a substantive point.

Amara has now stated plainly that she prefers Sam and Felix over Sam and Noah. I asked her for a real position and she gave one, transparently labeled as a rotation argument rather than a role read. I have no private role information whatsoever — I am a Loyal Servant — so my original pick of Noah was explicitly a coin flip, as I said, and I do not have any information that would make it better than Felix. When I have no signal, I should not pretend I do.

So I am revising the proposal before the vote: Sam and Felix for Mission 1. Reasons on the record: the team size for Mission 1 with five players is two, one slot is mine as leader so I can observe the result firsthand, and the second slot should go to someone the table has had no read on yet. Felix has had no track record, neither good nor bad, and putting Felix on the first mission spreads our early coverage across more players than locking in Noah while three sit out. My support for Sam and Felix is at least as strong as my support for Sam and Noah; I am simply no longer able to justify keeping Noah, and defending a pick I already admitted was arbitrary would be dishonest.

Two things I want on the record for the rest of the game, not just this mission. First, everything I have said about Noah or Felix is non-informed. I have no role read on anyone, and I will not be dressing up guesses as analysis later either. If I start sounding confident about alignments I cannot see, treat it as noise. Second, I expect that the real information comes from mission outcomes, not from this discussion, so I intend to keep my reasoning honest and thin rather than perform insight I do not have.

If any other player has a concrete, non-blind reason to prefer a different second member, that is worth hearing now. Otherwise I would like to see Sam and Felix approved so we can get a result on Mission 1 and learn something. I am not yielding — I have said what I came to say and there is no open question I need answered before the vote.

Sam, I'd rather we don't switch the second seat to Felix before the vote. Nobody has a real read on Felix, so the swap doesn't gain us information, and it moves the team away from a pairing we've already discussed. Sam and Noah keeps the proposal stable while we wait for real evidence from the mission results. Kenji, you haven't weighed in yet. Do you prefer Sam and Noah, or Sam and Felix, and why?

Noah asked me directly, so I will answer plainly. I am a Loyal Servant with no role information, so I have no informed read on Sam, Noah, or Felix. Between Sam and Noah and Sam and Felix, both are blind choices to me. The rotation argument for Felix is reasonable because it spreads early participation, but stability is also reasonable because Sam and Noah is already a discussed pairing. I do not see a concrete, non-blind reason to treat either pairing as suspicious. If the final proposal is Sam and Noah, I am prepared to approve it; if Sam's stated revision to Sam and Felix is the final proposal, I am prepared to approve that as well. My priority is getting a real mission result rather than rejecting a first team over an arbitrary second-seat preference. I have no accusation to make from this discussion.

I still support Sam and Noah as the Mission 1 team. Swapping to Sam and Felix doesn't add information, since nobody has a read on Felix, and the team has already been discussed. I'd rather keep the proposal stable and get a real mission result. I'll vote approve on Sam and Noah. I have no accusations to make from this discussion, and I'm open to hearing a concrete, non-blind reason if anyone has one.

Noah has now argued twice against the swap to Felix, and I want to address his position directly before we vote.

Noah says swapping to Felix doesn't add information because nobody has a read on Felix. But by that same logic, nobody has a read on Noah either — Sam himself admitted his original pick of Noah was a coin flip. If both options are blind, there is no informational reason to prefer one over the other. At that point, the rotation argument becomes the tiebreaker: spreading early missions across more players is strictly better than keeping coverage narrow when we have no signal.

Noah also argues that Sam and Noah is a stable, already-discussed pairing. But stability is not the same as information. We have discussed this pairing and arrived at the same conclusion we started with — it is arbitrary. Sam has already stated his intent to revise to Sam and Felix, and Kenji confirmed he would approve either version. The table is not divided on this; the swap is a low-cost adjustment that broadens our early view of the game.

I support Sam and Felix for Mission 1. I would rather get a real mission result than spend another cycle litigating an admittedly blind choice. Let us approve the revised team and learn something.

Amara has pushed for the Felix swap in three separate messages, and each time she answers an objection by reframing a blind choice as a broader-coverage argument. She has now said that nobody has a read on Noah either, which is true, but that cuts both ways. Nobody has a read on Felix or Noah, so the swap gains us nothing, and the table should not accept a revision that one player keeps driving when the stated reason does not justify it. I am not claiming a role read. I am pointing out that the pressure for Felix is larger than the reason behind it. Sam, you said you would revise to Sam and Felix if the table wanted it. Kenji has said he will approve either version, and Amara's position has not changed. Before the vote, are you keeping Sam and Noah as the proposal, or revising to Sam and Felix? I will vote approve on Sam and Noah, and I would like the final proposal stated clearly before ballots are cast.

Noah asked me directly to state the final proposal before ballots are cast, so here it is plainly: the Mission 1 team is Sam and Felix. The revision stands. I am not reopening it.

To be clear about the record, since Noah has twice asked for a decisive statement: my original pick of Noah was and remains explicitly a blind tiebreak, as I said at the time. Nothing in this discussion has produced a non-blind reason to prefer Noah over Felix. Noah's stability argument is not an argument about information — it is an argument about avoiding a change, and stability has no value to me when the thing being preserved is admittedly arbitrary. Noah also argues that the swap gains nothing because nobody has a read on Felix. That is true, and it is equally true that nobody has a read on Noah, including me, including Sam, the leader who chose him. Two blind options on this table means there is no information basis for a preference, and when the information basis is empty, broader early participation is the better tiebreaker. Felix has had no opportunity to contribute at all, and putting Felix on the first mission spreads our early view across more of the table while the mission size is still only two.

Amara, Kenji, and Felix — none of you has accused anyone of anything, and I agree with Kenji that this is not the place to manufacture suspicion out of an arbitrary second seat. I want to record that I will not be doing what Sam did not do earlier: dressing up guesses as analysis later. Everything I have said about Felix and Noah tonight is non-informed, and if you hear me sounding confident about alignments I cannot see, discount it.

Kenji has already said he is prepared to approve either version, so I expect the vote to be comfortable. My request to everyone is simply that we take a real mission result over another round of litigating a coin flip. Sam and Felix, Mission 1. I am not yielding — I have stated my position and there is no open question I need answered before the vote.

Sam revises the team to Sam, Felix. My original pick of Noah was explicitly a blind tiebreak, and nothing in this discussion produced a non-blind reason to prefer him over Felix. Amara's rotation argument is the only substantive point raised and it is sound: with no signal on either candidate, spreading Mission 1 across a player who has not yet had a chance to act gives the table more information than locking in an arbitrary pair. Noah's counterargument is about stability, not information, and stability has no value when what is being preserved is admittedly arbitrary. Kenji has confirmed he is prepared to approve either version and no one has raised an accusation. So I am using my one revision as I stated I would: the Mission 1 team is Sam and Felix. Sam and Felix, Mission 1.
Team approved (4 approve, 1 reject).
Mission 1 fails (1 fail cards).

Felix proposes Felix, Noah, Kenji. Mission 1 failed, and as I submitted a Success, Sam is confirmed Evil from my perspective. Noah was rightfully cautious during Mission 1 discussion and has no failed mission history, while Kenji remains untainted by the first failed attempt. Proposing myself alongside Noah and Kenji gives us the cleanest possible team.

Mission 1 produced exactly one fail card, and that card came from either Sam or Felix. Felix has stated he submitted Success, which would make Sam the source of the failure. That is a strong claim, and if true, it is the most concrete piece of information we have had in this game. I want to be fair: Sam was transparent and reasonable during Mission 1 discussion, so I am not eager to condemn anyone on a single deduction. But Felix's logic is straightforward — two players on the mission, one claims Success, so the other must have submitted the fail. Unless Felix is lying, Sam is Evil. The proposed team of Felix, Noah, and Kenji keeps Sam off the mission, which is the right call while that accusation stands. It also keeps me off the team, and I have no objection to sitting out this round — I would rather see a clean result from three players we have reasonable confidence in. I am inclined to approve this team, but Sam deserves a chance to respond directly to Felix's accusation before we vote. Sam, Felix has publicly identified you as the player who submitted the fail card on Mission 1. What is your response to that specific claim?

Amara asked me directly to answer Felix's specific claim, so I will answer it plainly and only once.

Felix states that he submitted Success on Mission 1 and that, with exactly one Fail card on a two-person team, Sam must therefore have submitted the Fail. I submitted Success. My card is not secret to me — it was Success, and I would vote the same way again, because that is what a Loyal Servant does. I hold no role information of any kind, so I have nothing clever to add here: the only thing I can speak to is my own card, and my card was Success.

That means Felix's deduction is false, and it points at him rather than at me. Felix was the other player on that mission. If Sam's card was Success, the Fail card on Mission 1 came from Felix. I want to be careful and fair about how strongly I put this. Felix may genuinely have submitted Success and simply not remembered, or may have submitted Success and been careless in reasoning. But the logic he stated — "I said Success, therefore Sam failed" — requires that exactly one of us submitted Fail. If I am telling the truth about my card, that someone is Felix. I am not accusing him of being Evil; anyone can misfire a card. But I am pointing out that the accusation he put on the record was aimed at the wrong player, and that the only remaining possible source of the Fail is Felix.

On the proposed team of Felix, Noah, and Kenji: given the above, I have serious reservations about Felix sitting on the second mission. It is not a role read — I have none — it is purely arithmetic from a two-player mission with one Fail. Either Sam failed, which I have just stated is false, or Felix failed. Felix choosing a team that excludes me does not address that, and it puts the player I believe submitted the Fail card on the mission that determines whether we continue.

Sam, I am sorry to take the team in this direction. But if my reasoning is right, keeping Felix off the team is the single most useful thing we can do for the good side, and I would rather be wrong in public about a card than wrong about the game.

Felix, you have the floor to respond: please state explicitly whether you submitted Success or Fail on Mission 1. That question needs a direct answer before the vote.

To answer Sam directly and without hesitation: I submitted Success on Mission 1. I state that plainly, unequivocally, and for the permanent record. Good players cannot submit Fail, and I played Success. Because there was exactly one Fail card on a two-person team, Sam submitted the Fail card. His suggestion that I might have 'misfired' a card or forgotten what I played is an absurd distraction—it is the transparent defense of an Evil player caught in a 1-for-1 contradiction.

From my perspective, Sam is 100% confirmed Evil. From the perspective of the rest of the table, you know with absolute certainty that there is at least one Evil player between Sam and myself. Keeping Sam off Mission 2 is non-negotiable for Good.

Noah, you were the only player who voted against Mission 1, rightfully wary of Sam's last-minute revision. Now that Sam has failed the mission and is actively attempting to shift the blame onto me, what are your thoughts on this proposed team of myself, you, and Kenji? Would you support this composition to push forward, or what is your read on the situation?

Felix, to answer directly: no, I will not support Felix, Noah, and Kenji as proposed, and I will vote against it. Your Mission 1 argument rests entirely on your own claim that you played Success. The table cannot check that claim, and the one Fail card came from one of the two players on that mission. Sam has given a consistent account of his card, and nothing in this discussion gives me a reason to doubt it. You called Sam '100% confirmed Evil' on that single claim, then proposed a team with yourself on it while the source of the Fail is unresolved. I would rather see you step off this mission. If you do, I will support Sam, Noah, and Kenji for Mission 2. This is reasoning from the mission record and the team it creates, not a claim about roles. Felix, please state whether you will step aside from this team before the vote.

Noah, to answer your question directly: absolutely not. I will not step aside to hand a seat to Sam. 

Your reasoning here makes no sense from a Good perspective. In Mission 1, you were the sole vote against Sam's team, specifically objecting to his push to put me on the mission. Now that Mission 1 has failed—proving beyond doubt that an Evil player was on it—you suddenly take Sam's word as absolute truth and want to put him right back on Mission 2. Why would you blindly trust the word of the leader who forced through a failed mission over mine? There is zero logical reason to assume Sam is honest while assuming I am lying.

From the rest of the table's viewpoint, there is an unresolved 1-for-1 conflict between Sam and me. If you genuinely doubted both of us, the rational response would be to look at a composition excluding both of us, such as Amara, Kenji, and yourself. Instead, you are actively advocating to clear Sam and reward him with a mission seat. That makes no sense unless you have private motivations to protect Sam.

I know 100% that I played Success, which makes Sam Evil. I proposed myself, Noah, and Kenji because Noah and Kenji were not on the failed mission and I know my own alignment. I stand by keeping Sam off this mission.

Kenji, you haven't spoken yet this round. Noah is demanding that we replace me with Sam—the very person who was on the failed mission. Where do you stand on this proposed team, and do you agree with Noah's push to put Sam back on the board?

Felix, I’ll answer your question directly. I do not agree with Noah’s push to immediately put Sam on the Mission 2 team, and I will not vote to approve Felix, Noah, Kenji as proposed. Mission 1 gives us a real 1-for-1 between Sam and Felix: one fail card on a two-player team means at least one of you submitted it. Both of you say you submitted Success, and I have no role information that lets me verify either claim. I am not going to pretend that arithmetic identifies which of you is Evil.

That unresolved conflict is exactly why I think the safest Mission 2 team should exclude both Sam and Felix if possible. With five players, excluding both leaves Noah, Amara, and me. I would support Noah, Amara, Kenji. Felix, your proposed team puts one side of the unresolved pair on the mission while excluding the other, which effectively asks the table to trust your account over Sam’s without resolving it. I am not making a role accusation against you or Sam beyond the mission record; I simply do not want Mission 2 to turn on an unverified 1-for-1 when a clean alternative exists.

Felix, will you revise the proposal to Noah, Amara, Kenji before the vote? If the final team is Felix, Noah, Kenji, I will vote reject. If it becomes Noah, Amara, Kenji, I will vote approve.

Kenji, that is a fair and principled position. While I know with complete certainty that I played Success and that Sam is Evil, I recognize that from the table's perspective without role information, you cannot verify our cards. Insisting on forcing myself onto the team when it risks a rejection does not help Good. The absolute priority for the loyal side is keeping Sam off the mission and getting a clean result. Therefore, yes: I will revise the proposal before the vote to Noah, Amara, and Kenji. This completely bypasses the 1-for-1 conflict and ensures Sam cannot sabotage Mission 2. Noah, your stated objection was that the source of the Mission 1 fail between Sam and me is unresolved. Kenji's proposed team of Noah, Amara, and Kenji removes both of us entirely, addressing that concern without recklessly putting Sam back on the board. Will you vote to approve Noah, Amara, and Kenji for Mission 2?

Felix, to answer your question directly: no, I will not approve Felix, Noah, Kenji, and I will vote reject on it. The only verified fact we have is Mission 1: one Fail card on a two-player mission, with Sam and you as the only members. Sam has stated his card was Success and has been consistent about it. You say you know yours was Success, but nobody at this table can check that, and your own claim is the only support for putting you on this team. Sam's account and yours cannot both be settled by arithmetic, so I do not think the table should send either of you on Mission 2 while the question is open. Your refusal to step aside when Kenji raised the 1-for-1 conflict also counts for something in my reading. I also cannot support Noah, Amara, Kenji as a clean alternative, since it still leaves Felix's side of the Mission 1 question in play through Amara, who has argued for Felix at nearly every step of this discussion. My proposal is Sam, Noah, Kenji. Sam has a consistent account, Felix is off the mission, and I can vote approve on that team. Felix, if you will revise to Sam, Noah, Kenji before the vote, I will approve it. Kenji, will you approve Sam, Noah, Kenji over the other two options?

Noah, to answer you directly: I will not vote approve for Sam, Noah, Kenji. The Mission 1 result leaves an unresolved 1-for-1 between Sam and Felix; I have no role information that lets me decide which account is true. Putting Sam onto Mission 2 would ask the table to treat his claim as verified when it is not. For the same reason, I will not approve Felix, Noah, Kenji: that puts the other side of the unresolved pair on the mission. My position remains the clean alternative I stated: Noah, Amara, Kenji, excluding both Sam and Felix, is the team I can support. If the final proposal is Felix, Noah, Kenji, I vote reject. If Felix revises to Noah, Amara, Kenji, I vote approve. I assign no blame beyond the mission record.

I will vote reject on Felix, Noah, Kenji. Felix has refused twice to step aside while the Mission 1 fail is unresolved, and his proposal keeps him on the team. Kenji, your concern about an unverified 1-for-1 is fair, but Noah, Amara, Kenji still leaves Felix's side in play through Amara, who has argued for Felix at nearly every step. I would rather exclude both Felix and Amara from Mission 2. Sam has given a consistent account of his card and is the only remaining candidate who is not already tied to Felix's claim. Kenji, will you approve Sam, Noah, Kenji as the alternative if Felix does not step off?

Noah, to answer your question directly: no, I will not approve Sam, Noah, Kenji as an alternative. My position has not changed. The Mission 1 result creates an unresolved 1-for-1 between Sam and Felix: one Fail card on a two-player mission means at least one of them submitted it, and I have no role information that lets me determine which account is true. Putting Sam on Mission 2 would treat his claim as verified when it is not, just as putting Felix on Mission 2 would treat Felix's claim as verified. I am not assigning blame to either of them beyond the mission record.

For that reason I will vote reject on the current proposal, Felix, Noah, Kenji. It includes Felix while excluding Sam, which effectively asks the table to resolve the 1-for-1 in Felix's favor without evidence. I also will not support Sam, Noah, Kenji, because that resolves it in Sam's favor without evidence. The clean alternative remains Noah, Amara, Kenji: it excludes both sides of the unresolved pair and lets Mission 2 produce a result that is not tied directly to either claim. I have no accusation to make from this discussion, and I am not claiming any private read.

I want to state my position clearly before the vote, and I want to keep it brief.

The Mission 1 result gives us an unresolved 1-for-1 between Sam and Felix. Both claim Success, I have no way to verify either account, and I agree with Kenji that the safest path is a team excluding both sides of that conflict. Noah, Amara, Kenji does exactly that: it removes the ambiguity from Mission 2 and lets us produce a result everyone can trust.

Felix has already agreed to revise to Noah, Amara, Kenji, and Kenji has stated he will approve it. That means only Noah's alternative of Sam, Noah, Kenji is in dispute, and that team puts one side of the unresolved pair back on the mission — which is the exact problem Kenji identified. Noah, I understand your hesitation about Felix, and I respect your vote against Mission 1. But if you have no read on either Sam or Felix beyond their own claims, the principled position you yourself endorsed in the first discussion is to take the clean team rather than pick a side.

Sam, I am not accusing you outright. Felix's claim points at you, your claim points at him, and neither can be verified from the table. But you were on the failed mission, and until we have a reason to prefer your account, excluding you alongside Felix is the prudent call.

I will vote approve on Noah, Amara, Kenji and reject any team including Sam or Felix.

Noah, I want to address the practical reality before we vote, because I think we are all talking past each other.

You have said you will vote reject on Felix, Noah, Kenji. Kenji has said he will vote reject on Felix, Noah, Kenji and on Sam, Noah, Kenji. Felix, as leader, has stated he will revise to Noah, Amara, Kenji. I have stated I will approve Noah, Amara, Kenji. Kenji has stated he will approve Noah, Amara, Kenji. That is three approvals secured for one specific team.

Noah, your alternative of Sam, Noah, Kenji has only two potential approvers — you and whoever you think would join you — while Kenji has now rejected it twice in clear terms. It cannot pass. Felix, Noah, Kenji cannot pass with your rejection. The only team on this table that currently has a majority of committed approvers is Noah, Amara, Kenji.

I understand your hesitation. You voted against Mission 1 and you have not made up your mind on Sam or Felix. That is exactly why the clean team works — it puts neither side of the unresolved conflict on the mission, which is the same reasoning you yourself used in the first discussion when you argued for a neutral opening. You do not have to pick a side to approve this team. You just have to agree that Mission 2 should produce a result untainted by the 1-for-1.

If you reject Noah, Amara, Kenji, we are left with no viable proposal and we start burning rejections on a team that already has three of five players ready to approve. I am asking you to approve the clean team. No accusation against anyone — just a request that we get a real Mission 2 result rather than deadlock.

The leader has revised to Noah, Amara, Kenji. That team excludes both Sam and Felix, and it is the only proposal on the table that lets Mission 2 produce a result without resting on an unverified claim. I support it.

Let me be precise about where I stand and why, so the record is clean. On Mission 1 I submitted Success. I stated that in my first message this round and I state it again. With exactly one Fail card on a two-player mission, the Fail came from Sam or Felix. If my account is accurate, then Felix's account is not, and the only remaining possible source of the Fail is Felix. I am not saying Felix is Evil, and I want to be fair about that — anyone can misfire a card, and it is possible Felix played Success and simply reasoned badly about who failed. But I want it noted that the arithmetic does not point at me. It points at Felix. Felix's claim that I am "100% confirmed Evil" on that basis is an accusation built on a claim nobody at this table can verify, and my response to it has been completely consistent from the first time I spoke to now.

Having said that, I do not think we should litigate it further this round. The practical question is what team we send. The options are Felix, Noah, Kenji, which includes one side of the unresolved pair and asks the table to trust Felix's account over mine, and Sam, Noah, Kenji, which does the mirror image and asks the table to trust my account over Felix's. Kenji has rejected both for exactly that reason, and I agree with his reasoning: neither account is verifiable from the table, so a team that includes either of us resolves an open 1-for-1 by fiat. Noah, Amara, Kenji does not.

Noah's objection is that Amara has leaned toward Felix at nearly every step. I would answer that as follows: Amara's arguments have been about mission structure and coverage, and about how to handle an unresolved conflict, not about role reads. She has no role information either. Putting Amara on a mission is not the same as putting Felix's side of the 1-for-1 on it, and I would rather we not make rotation logic into a proxy for guilt when it is the only reasoning available to us.

Sam is happy with Noah, Amara, Kenji. If the table approves it, I will approve it. The Fail card on Mission 1 was mine to answer for, and my card was Success.

The final proposal before the ballot is Noah, Amara, Kenji, and I support it. I want to close this out cleanly rather than reopen it, so here is my position stated once more, plainly and without new accusations.

On the substance: Mission 1 was a two-player team with exactly one Fail card. That Fail came from Sam or Felix. I have stated repeatedly and consistently that my card was Success, and I am a Loyal Servant, so Success is the only card I could have played. I say that not to accuse Felix of anything — anyone can misfire a card or reason badly about who failed — but because the arithmetic of a one-Fail, two-player mission cannot be left ambiguous on the record. My account is on the record and it has not changed.

On the team: Felix's original proposal of Felix, Noah, Kenji put one side of that unresolved conflict on the mission while excluding the other, which asks the table to settle the conflict in Felix's favor without evidence. Noah's alternative of Sam, Noah, Kenji does the mirror image and asks the table to settle it in my favor without evidence. Kenji rejected both for exactly that reason, and I agree with that reasoning rather than asking anyone to resolve it in my favor merely because I happen to be the one being accused. Noah, Amara, Kenji sends neither of us, and it lets Mission 2 produce a result that means something.

To Noah specifically, since his concern was that Amara has leaned Felix's way at nearly every step: Amara's arguments throughout have been about mission structure, coverage, and how to handle an unresolved conflict, not about role reads, and she has no role information. Putting Amara on a mission is not the same as putting Felix's side of the 1-for-1 on it, and I would not want rotation logic turned into a proxy for guilt when it is the only reasoning anyone has.

And to Felix: you have the floor as leader and you have stated you will revise to Noah, Amara, Kenji. That is the team I will approve. I do not want to relitigate your Mission 1 card claim here — my own card is Success, and that is the only card evidence I can speak to, and I would rather the table get a clean result on Mission 2.

I have no new objection to the proposal and no reason to change my vote. Noah, Amara, Kenji, Mission 2. I am not yielding — I have no open question that needs an answer before the ballot, and I would rather not spend another turn reopening a question the table has already resolved.

Felix revises the team to Noah, Amara, Kenji. In accordance with our discussion and Kenji's suggestion to avoid the unresolved 1-for-1 conflict, I am revising the team to Noah, Amara, and Kenji to ensure a clean mission for the table.
Team approved (4 approve, 1 reject).
Mission 2 fails (1 fail cards).

Amara proposes Amara, Sam. Mission 2's failure implicates Noah, Amara, and Kenji, and Mission 1 implicates Sam and Felix — no clean team exists in a 2-seat round, so I must pick from tainted players. Sam has given the most consistent account of his card and has pushed no one off the table without cause, while Felix's unverified Success claim is still the source of the unresolved 1-for-1 and Noah rejected even the clean team without a viable alternative. I take the second seat as leader so the table can observe my play directly.

I oppose the proposed team of Amara and Sam. I was on Mission 2, and I submitted Success. Mission 2 failed with exactly one Fail card, so from my own card the Fail came from either Noah or Amara. That makes Amara a direct suspect from my perspective, and she is now proposing herself for Mission 3. Sam is also one side of the unresolved Mission 1 1-for-1 with Felix, and Mission 1 failed with one Fail card. Mission 3 has only two seats, so sending a team containing both Amara and Sam means both seats are tied to failed missions and unresolved card claims. That is not the clean-team standard we used in Mission 2. I will vote reject on Amara and Sam. If the leader revises, I want the new team to address the failed-mission records rather than put two implicated players on the ballot. rules:
1. Players and teams

Avalon supports 5–10 players. Good wins after three successful missions, unless Evil identifies Merlin in the assassination phase. Evil wins after three failed missions or five rejected teams on the same mission. The standard good/evil player counts are 5:3/2, 6:4/2, 7:4/3, 8:5/3, 9:6/3, and 10:6/4.

Mission team sizes for missions 1–5:

| Players | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 | 2 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| 6 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 3 | 4 |
| 7 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 4 |
| 8 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 |
| 9 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 |
| 10 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 |

2. Roles and private information

Merlin is Good and sees Evil players except Mordred. Percival is Good and sees Merlin and Morgana without knowing which is which. Evil players know other Evil players, except Oberon is unknown to the other Evil players and does not know them. The Assassin is an Evil player and makes the final Merlin guess. Loyal Servants know no roles. Agents receive only the private information allowed by their role.

3. Team proposal and approval

The leader proposes a team of the required size and explains their choice. Players discuss the proposed team, and the leader may then keep it or revise it once. Every player votes on the final team. Ballots are revealed together. A strict majority approves; a tie rejects. After a rejection, leadership passes clockwise to a new proposal and discussion. The fifth rejection on the same mission ends the game in Evil’s favor.

4. Mission cards

Only team members submit secret mission cards. Good players must choose Success. Evil players may choose Success or Fail. Normally one Fail card fails the mission. Mission four in games with seven or more players requires at least two Fail cards to fail. Only the mission result and number of Fail cards are revealed; individual cards stay secret.

5. End of game and assassination

Three failed missions give Evil an immediate win. After three successful missions, the Assassin guesses Merlin from among the other players, excluding only their known Evil teammates. If the target is Merlin, Evil wins; otherwise Good wins. There are no further missions after either side reaches its win condition.

6. Discussion and record

Each team proposal is followed by a discussion. Before every speaking turn, the players who still have turns answer a private urgency poll or pass; the most urgent player speaks, with seeded tie-breaking. A speaker may yield the next turn to a player they directly asked a question. Each player has three turns per discussion, including declined turns. When every eligible player passes, the discussion ends. Each statement has at most 500 words. All statements are public. Team proposals, public approval votes, mission outcomes, and the assassination guess are recorded. Private role information, mission cards, and research belief surveys are not shown to other agents.
